content: The National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) is a nonprofit organization headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota. It manages the federally funded registry of volunteer hematopoietic cell donors in the United States. As of October 2007, the registry included over 6.8 million potential donors who have volunteered to donate hematopoietic cells for patients requiring a transplant. Since its establishment in 1986, the NMDP has facilitated 30,000 successful transplants by December 3, 2007. Additionally, the registry includes more than 69,000 umbilical cord blood units, which can also serve as a source of hematopoietic cells for transplantation. In October 2006, the NMDP was awarded a federal contract to manage the national cord blood registry in the United States. Hematopoietic cell transplants are a critical treatment for various life-threatening conditions, including leukemia, lymphoma, aplastic anemia, certain immune system disorders, and genetic diseases. Hematopoietic cells, which are blood-forming stem cells, can be sourced from bone marrow, umbilical cord blood, or peripheral blood stem cells (PBSCs). These cells are a type of adult stem cell capable of differentiating into red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Large registries of unrelated donors are essential because only about 30% of patients in need of a hematopoietic cell transplant can find a suitable HLA-matched donor within their family. For the remaining 70%, an unrelated donor is required. The probability of two random individuals being HLA-matched is less than 1 in 20,000, necessitating a large pool of volunteer donors for a registry to be effective. The NMDP operates by coordinating hematopoietic cell transplants through a global network of affiliated organizations, primarily hospitals. These organizations collaborate with the NMDP to facilitate the collection and transfer of donated bone marrow or cord blood. When an adult volunteer donor registers with the NMDP, their HLA information is recorded in the NMDP’s database, along with their contact information, so they can be reached if matched with a patient. The NMDP also maintains a registry of over 69,000 cord blood units stored at 24 affiliated cord blood banks worldwide (as of October 2007). Physicians searching for a donor on behalf of a patient submit the patient’s HLA tissue type to the NMDP. The organization then searches its database for a matching donor. If a match is found, the NMDP contacts the potential donor, informs them of the match, and educates them about the donation process. If the donor agrees to proceed, they undergo a medical examination, including blood tests for infectious diseases. If the donor meets all requirements, their bone marrow or PBSCs are collected and transported to the patient via courier. The NMDP is part of Bone Marrow Donors Worldwide (BMDW), an organization based in Leiden, The Netherlands, that facilitates communication among global registries. There are approximately 10 million volunteer hematopoietic cell donors worldwide. Most national registries, including the NMDP, have access to these international donors through the BMDW or bilateral agreements. Although the NMDP is based in the United States, it has extensive international connections. Over 40% of the transplants it arranges involve either a foreign donor or a foreign patient. The NMDP collaborates with seven donor centers outside the United States, located in The Netherlands, Israel, Sweden, Norway, and Germany (three centers). It is also affiliated with 17 transplant centers outside the United States. In addition to the NMDP, there are three smaller registries in the United States. The Caitlin Raymond International Registry, based at UMass Memorial Medical Center in Massachusetts, has approximately 64,000 adult volunteer donors and access to 10,000 cord blood units. The American Bone Marrow Donor Registry (ABMDR), based in Mandeville, Louisiana, has about 32,000 adult volunteer donors. The Caitlin Raymond International Registry serves as the search center for the ABMDR. The Gift of Life Bone Marrow Foundation, based in Boca Raton, Florida, focuses on recruiting donors of Jewish ethnic ancestry. It has registered approximately 110,000 volunteer donors and has access to 400 cord blood units. In May 2004, the Gift of Life Bone Marrow Foundation partnered with the NMDP, becoming an Associate Donor Registry. Similarly, in July 2007, the Caitlin Raymond International Registry became affiliated with the NMDP. The NMDP receives approximately $23 million annually from the U.S. government through the Health Resources and Services Administration. Additional funding is provided by the U.S. Navy. The program also generates income from donations, fees charged to donors for tissue typing (approximately $50 as of 2006, with waivers for some minority groups), fees for in-depth database searches (initial searches are free, but full searches can cost several thousand dollars), and fees charged to transplanting hospitals once a match is found and the stem cells are transferred. The fee for the transfer of stem cells is approximately $21,000, which is higher than the fees charged by other registries in the U.S. and abroad. The total cost of a completed transplant, including hospital and medical expenses, can range from $100,000 to $250,000. The NMDP also compensates affiliated donor centers and recruitment groups for each new donor they register.
